name: Isolated limb infusion (melphalan +/- dactinomycin)
cyclesNote: Single regional-chemotherapy procedure for extensive or bulky unresectable in-transit / satellite melanoma confined to a limb, performed at experienced centers. Delivered as a one-time low-flow isolated limb infusion (or isolated limb perfusion) with tourniquet-isolated limb circulation and mild hyperthermia; not a repeatedly cycled systemic regimen. A second procedure may be considered for later limb-confined recurrence at the treating team's discretion.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Regional cytotoxic chemotherapy for limb-confined in-transit melanoma; not biomarker-selected and used regardless of BRAF status. Selection is anatomic (bulky or numerous in-transit / satellite lesions limited to one extremity, not amenable to simple excision or intralesional therapy).

premedications.name: Systemic anticoagulation
premedications.notes: Heparin during limb isolation, per procedural protocol; reverse as indicated after infusion.

supportiveCare: Limb toxicity monitoring (Wieberdink scale) for regional skin/muscle reaction, edema, and compartment syndrome; elevate and observe the limb after the procedure.
Watch for systemic melphalan leak (myelosuppression, nausea) if limb isolation is incomplete; serial limb and systemic drug leak monitoring during the infusion.
Creatine kinase trend as a marker of regional muscle injury.
monitoring: limb perfusion, temperature, and Wieberdink toxicity grade during and after the procedure
CBC after the procedure to detect systemic melphalan exposure from isolation leak
creatine kinase and renal function for regional muscle injury / myoglobin load
clinical response of in-transit lesions over the following weeks

doseModificationRules.text: Melphalan dose is scaled to measured limb volume (mg per litre of limb), with a lower per-litre dose typically used for the lower limb than the upper limb, and adjusted for ideal body weight in some protocols. Physician / regional-therapy team sets the exact dose.

drugs.name: Melphalan
drugs.notes: Regional low-flow isolated limb infusion. Dose is calculated from measured limb volume, roughly 7 to 10 mg per litre of limb for a lower limb and a higher per-litre dose for an upper limb (some protocols correct for ideal body weight). The flat 40 mg shown here is a representative single-procedure total for a typical lower limb and MUST be replaced by the limb-volume-based dose set by the regional-therapy team. Delivered into the isolated limb circulation under tourniquet with mild hyperthermia, not systemically. Own-wording summary; not a verbatim protocol copy.

drugs.name: Dactinomycin (actinomycin-D)
drugs.notes: Optional second agent added to the melphalan infusate at some centers, dosed by limb volume (roughly 75 to 100 micrograms per litre of limb). The flat 0.5 mg shown is a representative single-procedure total and MUST be replaced by the limb-volume-based dose. Omit where melphalan is used alone. Own-wording summary; not a verbatim protocol copy.
